name: Domestic food-grade soybean and mung bean for soy foods and plant drinks
what: Contract-grown, non-GM, food-grade soybeans (and in a second step mung beans) sold to soy-milk, tofu and plant-drink makers, replacing part of the imported beans behind the protein people already eat. Step one is a buyer-led value-chain taskforce on the model of the EU fava bean roadmap: a barrier map from seed to buyer, a farm-economics test of two or three farm types (Red River Delta winter crop after rice; upland soybean in Lam Dong (former Dak Nong)), and a price and volume series
why_vietnam: Soy foods carry about 181,000 t of protein a year (2023) on beans that are 97.5% imported, nearly ten times what new routes deliver in 2035 on the benchmark path (DIE-07; ch22). It is the only in-scope route found that raises the domestic-input share of protein people already eat at that scale: the 2010 soybean area (205 kha) at 2.0 to 2.5 t/ha would give 410 to 510 kt of beans, 76% to 95% of 2025 food soybean use (our calculation; AQF-20; MAC-04). A named buyer markets non-GM and breeds for it: Vinasoy holds 2,072 soybean lines and VINASOY 05 yields above 2.5 t/ha at Cu Jut; its parent plans to invest in soybean raw-material areas in 2026 (AIB-06). Consumers pay a large premium for non-GM soy milk (NOV-08). Land is being released from rice (654 kha by 2030; NTS-15), and MAE asks to reduce import dependence through domestic raw-material areas (SEC-02)
must_be_true: A farm margin for soybean in rotation at least equal to maize or vegetables at a price buyers will pay; buyers pay a premium over imported non-GM food beans that covers the gap (domestic 25,000 to 30,000 VND/kg against 13,000 to 15,000 for imports in 2024, AQF-20; or 1.4 to 1.7 times the 2023 Canadian import unit value of USD 686/t, our calculation from SEC-05); contract yields of 2.0 t/ha or more against a national average of about 1.3 t/ha (PCV-007); drying, storage and grading capacity near growing areas
kill_tests: The farm-economics test shows soybean below maize or rice margins at any price buyers accept; Vinasoy and two tofu or plant-drink makers will not sign conditional contracts for at least 5,000 t a year (our threshold); imported identity-preserved non-GM beans land at under two thirds of the domestic contract price for two years running; contract yields stay below 2.0 t/ha over three seasons
first_customers: Vinasoy (soy milk); ToFu House and other industrial tofu makers; plant-drink makers looking for local mung bean (T10 buyers such as Vinamilk)
partners: Vinasoy Soybean Applied Research Centre (VSAC); MAE crop and extension agencies; provinces releasing rice land; Can Tho University and other groups that study rice-upland rotations (our suggestion; not contacted)
horizon: 1 to 5 years (farm-economics test and taskforce in year 1; contract areas in years 2 to 5)
capital_note: Low fixed capital: seed multiplication, extension, drying and storage near growing areas, and working capital for crop purchase. Not costed; the farm-economics test sets the size. Best owned by the buyer (contract farming) with public extension and seed support, not venture capital
